architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Using the measured 120-130 C level change relative to the same-lattice unmodified reactive-core reference, accept exactly one registered level hypothesis if the result is within 3.4 percentage points of its prediction: H-LEVEL-DILUTE at -42.76%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC at 17.24%, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC at -72.76%. The candidate processing-window levels at 120 and 130 C must also be reported directly.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The 120 and 130 C viscosity levels are measured directly in the selected resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry, so those primary levels stay within the measurement capability of the selected experiment. They do not depend on transferring the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared shape. E_eta is a fitted rheological descriptor within the candidate sweep, not evidence of a molecular mechanism. The selected M-SWEEP is required because prior shared-shape support for this chemistry family is unvalidated.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change is outside [-46.16%, -39.36%]. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level change is at or below -42.76%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if the measured level change is at or above -42.76%. If the result is not within 3.4 percentage points of any one prediction, none of the three registered level hypotheses is accepted; this falsifies their clean discrimination at this composition rather than establishing a molecular mechanism.
hypotheses_left_entangled: AC1920/TK100 interaction versus an unregistered whole-formulation effect
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT to quantify between-preparation realization-state spread, then use matched single-axis candidates if axis-specific attribution is required.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C, expressed as percent change relative to the same-lattice unmodified reactive-core reference; the sweep also reports the fitted rheological temperature-response descriptor E_eta.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 is the smallest dual-axis intervention in the deterministic top intervention family and remains within the externally supported modifier region. M-SWEEP directly measures the failure-mode quantity at 120 and 130 C, separates the three preregistered formulation-level level predictions in principle, and avoids unsupported transfer of the unmodified thermal-response shape. The primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity measured in the same chemistry family; it is measured directly in the selected candidate, while E_eta is only a fitted rheological descriptor.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: Followed the Proposer and Skeptic on selecting direct M-SWEEP over the deterministic VOI-tied M-ANCHOR cards. Followed the Robustness Adjudicator in breaking the deterministic tie toward S1C41 and in treating the chemistry audit as scientifically decisive despite its advisory enforcement. The Skeptic's objection that the 3.4% criterion is not attainable with one preparation changes interpretation and requires repeatability characterization, but does not change the experiment choice.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The candidate is a dual-axis AC1920/TK100 intervention, so the sweep tests formulation-level predictions but cannot isolate either modifier axis or their interaction.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the 120-130 C level because those temperatures are measured directly; high if the result is interpreted through the previously validated unmodified shared shape or as a molecular mechanism.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The catalogued M-SWEEP discrimination resolution is 3.4%; direct readings at 120 and 130 C avoid temperature-shape reconstruction error.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High: original matched-temperature repeatability showed approximately 2.80-3.57x max/min spread and sample CVs of 0.585 at 120 C and 0.541 at 130 C. A single preparation cannot reliably resolve a 3.4% chemistry difference; independent repeats and comparable references are scientifically necessary for strong adjudication.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original PUR reactive-hot-melt formulation family centered on the E2 reactive core, with E1-E3 temperature sweeps and a separate E1 +P chemical-perturbation check. The intended experiment would stay inside this family by retaining that reactive-core family while testing a registered modifier-axis candidate, but use of shared-shape calibration remains conditional on the chemistry audit; a direct sweep is the safer measurement plan until support is confirmed.
planner.failure_mode: The modified candidate may fall outside the processing-viscosity window at the 120-130 C application temperature, with realization-state variability large enough to obscure chemistry effects.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E2 temperature sweeps measured mean viscosity levels of 4316 at 120 C and 3322 at 130 C, while the three-run spread was large: sample CV 0.585 and 0.541, with max/min ratios of 3.57 and 3.34, respectively.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only two original formulations have measured 120 C holds: E1 has SI_15_to_60 = 0.095 and E5 has SI_15_to_60 = 0.515, with no matched hold trajectory for the E2 reactive-core anchor or for a modified candidate. The time coordinate is therefore sparse and confounded with formulation, despite the temperature-response coordinate having multiple 80-130 C sweeps.
measurement_requirements: Directly measure the candidate viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments, including the 120 and 130 C decision temperatures, rather than reconstructing those levels from a one-point anchor.

Use at least three independently prepared realizations or otherwise quantify preparation-state spread so chemistry-induced level changes are separable from the observed E2-scale repeatability variation.

Report the realized viscosity level relative to the same-lattice unmodified reactive-core reference and compare it with the pre-registered dilution, association, and plasticization predictions using the stated discrimination threshold.

Because the isothermal time trajectory is least resolved, include a matched 120 C hold with measurements at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and at least two independent repeats if time stability is part of the candidate decision.
planner.scientific_question: At matched processing temperature, does the modifier change the realized viscosity level only through inert dilution, elevate it above dilution as predicted by acrylic association, or depress it below dilution through plasticization? A directly measured candidate temperature sweep with controlled repeats must distinguish H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC beyond the stated measurement resolution.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate is outside the chemistry family in which the shared thermal-response shape was validated, so a one-point shared-shape reconstruction is not scientifically supported. M-SWEEP avoids that transfer assumption by measuring the candidate response directly; its processing-window level is therefore admissible as a direct observable, while E_eta remains a fitted rheological descriptor rather than a mechanistic activation energy.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: The directly measured 120-130 C level change relative to the same-lattice unmodified reactive-core reference falls within the 3.4% discrimination resolution of exactly one registered prediction: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. The matching hypothesis is supported for S1C41 and the directly measured processing-window level is reported.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -42.76% by more than 3.4%. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level is at or below -42.76%, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.76%. A result clearly closer to either alternative prediction supports that alternative instead.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: If the measured level does not fall within 3.4% of one prediction, the registered level hypotheses are not cleanly discriminated at this composition. The result should be treated as intermediate or as evidence that realization-state variability, model resolution, or an unregistered modifier effect dominates; the directly measured temperature response still establishes the candidate's processing-window level and tests whether its thermal shape differs from the local reference.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the 120 and 130 C processing-window temperatures, together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Although it has the highest deterministic VOI, it reconstructs the decision-temperature level through a shared shape that has not been verified for the resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry. The audit is advisory rather than binding, but this creates unsupported extrapolation and makes the primary observable model-dependent.

It also directly measures the modified chemistry and can separate the same three level hypotheses, but it uses a larger acrylic-like modifier burden without a corresponding information advantage over S1C41.

It directly measures the poorly resolved time-drift coordinate, but its primary observable does not return the processing-window viscosity level and cannot separate the three registered level hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41 retains the E2 reactive-core proportions while using the smallest dual-axis intervention in the deterministic top family: 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100, both within externally supported regions. M-SWEEP is preferred over the nominally higher-VOI anchor because the local rheological regularity has not been measured in this modified chemistry. Direct measurement at 120 and 130 C maximizes interpretability, tests the actual failure-mode quantity, and separates all three registered level hypotheses without relying on an unverified shape transfer.

robustness_adjudication.chemistry_domain_objection_reasoning: S1C41 is marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated with no verified shape transfer, and the local shared thermal-response shape was measured only in the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family. Because the audit enforcement is advisory, the M-ANCHOR cards remain selectable, but the chemistry-domain facts make them scientifically unsupported for the primary processing-window observable. The direct M-SWEEP measures 120-130 C viscosity in the candidate chemistry and is therefore the required choice over M-ANCHOR; weight sensitivity cannot repair an observable outside its measured chemistry support.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal S1C41::M-SWEEP departs from the deterministic tied top set, which consists of five S1C41/S1C46/S1C51/S1C56/S1C61 M-ANCHOR cards. This departure is scientifically justified because M-ANCHOR reconstructs the processing-window level through a shared thermal-response shape that has not been validated for the resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry, whereas M-SWEEP measures the decision temperatures directly.
residual_decision_risk: Preparation-state variability may remain large enough to obscure chemistry effects unless at least three independent candidate realizations and comparable unmodified references are measured.
The dual-axis S1C41 intervention cannot causally isolate AC1920 from TK100 or their interaction.
The chemistry-domain support for shared-shape transfer remains unverified until the direct sweep supplies evidence for this modified family.
The M-SWEEP temperature descriptor E_eta remains a fitted rheological descriptor rather than molecular-mechanism evidence.
The experiment does not resolve the sparse 120 C thermal-hold trajectory or establish hot-hold stability.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is that the stated 3.4% M-SWEEP discrimination resolution is not attainable with min_repeats equal to 1 given the observed 2.80-3.57x matched-temperature realization spread. This does not change which experiment should be run: the Skeptic explicitly recommends retaining the direct M-SWEEP. It changes how its result may be interpreted and requires at least three independently prepared candidate realizations with comparably characterized same-lattice unmodified references before applying the discrimination criterion. The sweep can establish directly measured processing-window levels and a rheological temperature descriptor, but without repeatability control it cannot reliably attribute small level differences to chemistry or accept a registered level hypothesis. Dual-axis S1C41 also cannot isolate AC1920 from TK100, so any result supports only formulation-level phenomenological predictions, not a molecular mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The deterministic tied top set is unchanged in all 29 re-weighting scenarios: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, the top-set mean Jaccard is 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary is null. No tested scaling of budget efficiency, decision relevance, extrapolation risk, hypothesis discrimination, measurement interpretability, process state risk, or uncertainty reduction changes the deterministic ranking. These perturbations are defensible as sensitivity tests of the transparent VOI score, but they do not make the tied M-ANCHOR cards scientifically preferable because weight re-scaling cannot repair their unsupported chemistry-domain shape transfer. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is 0.002292, but the proposed direct sweep remains preferable on applicability and observability grounds rather than score margin.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The directly measured 120-130 C viscosity level stays inside the measurement capability of M-SWEEP but not inside the previously validated shared-shape chemistry support: S1C41 is resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 with modified_chemistry_unvalidated status and no verified shape transfer. Directly measuring the full 80-130 C sweep is therefore required before any shape-transfer or M-ANCHOR claim is made. E_eta remains a fitted rheological descriptor, not molecular-mechanism evidence.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The nominal M-SWEEP threshold is 3.4%, derived from a fitted-curve residual, but the specified protocol has min_repeats = 1 and does not quantify preparation-state spread. The upstream repeatability evidence shows orders-of-magnitude larger matched-temperature realization variation than 3.4%, so the experiment may return a number but cannot credibly determine whether departure from -42.76% or proximity to the alternative predictions is caused by chemistry. At least three independently prepared realizations, with the same-lattice unmodified reference characterized comparably, are required for the criterion to be operationally falsifiable.
leakage_findings: No reliance on an unmeasured experimental outcome is evident.

The claim that the sweep establishes acrylic association or plasticization as a molecular mechanism exceeds what the rheological level measurement can establish; it can only test the registered formulation-level predictions.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could support only a phenomenological whole-formulation level pattern, not the claimed acrylic-association or two-axis mechanism attribution.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15% and TK100 is 5%. Although the registered level predictions for H-LEVEL-DILUTE (-42.76%), H-LEVEL-ASSOC (17.24%), and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC (-72.76%) are numerically separated, the experiment cannot attribute any observed departure from dilution specifically to acrylic association rather than to TK100, an interaction between the axes, or an unregistered resin effect. A causal interpretation of the acrylic_like axis is therefore unavailable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Apparent falsification or acceptance of any of the three level hypotheses could instead reflect preparation-state variation, leaving the claimed discrimination unsupported.
objections.objection: The M-SWEEP card specifies min_repeats = 1 and the proposal uses a 3.4% discrimination threshold, but the upstream E2 repeatability evidence reports 2.80-3.57x realization spread at matched processing temperatures, with sample CVs of 0.585 at 120 C and 0.541 at 130 C. A single preparation cannot establish a 3.4% candidate-versus-reference difference or reliably meet the stated falsification criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A fitted thermal-response descriptor could be overinterpreted as mechanistic evidence, although it can still describe the candidate's rheological response.
objections.objection: The primary processing-window level at 120 and 130 C is directly measured by M-SWEEP, so the level observable itself is interpretable. However, the proposal also presents E_eta from a regression of ln(eta) versus 1/T as part of the primary observable. E_eta is a fitted descriptor with model assumptions and is not a directly measured molecular activation energy; the protocol cannot by itself establish a chemical mechanism from this descriptor.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that the unmodified shared shape already applies to AC1920/TK100 would be unsupported; only the directly measured candidate curve can support the level result.
objections.objection: S1C41 is classified as modified_chemistry_unvalidated in chemistry family resin_modified:ac1920+tk100, with no prior_verified_shape_transfer. The unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared thermal-response shape therefore does not support one-point reconstruction for this candidate. M-SWEEP appropriately measures 80-130 C directly and does not reuse that shape to obtain the processing-window level, but the candidate remains outside the previously measured chemistry support until this sweep supplies direct evidence.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment cannot support any claim about hot-hold drift or stability improvement, even if it discriminates the three static level predictions.
objections.objection: The proposal correctly lists all three registered level hypotheses as separated, and their predictions are farther apart than the nominal 3.4% M-SWEEP resolution. However, the experiment does not address the separate stability hypotheses or the least-resolved isothermal time trajectory. The upstream record states that E2 has no original 120 C hold and that E1 and E5 hold behavior is strongly formulation dependent.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Mechanistic language could be reported as established when the experiment supports only formulation-level prediction discrimination.
objections.objection: No outcome leakage is evident: the proposal uses the registered S1C41 composition and pre-result predictions, and the direct sweep does not require knowledge of a future result. The scope concern is limited to the statement that the experiment separates 'acrylic association' and 'plasticization'; the rheological level measurement can test the registered phenomenological predictions but cannot establish those molecular mechanisms.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct M-SWEEP rather than M-ANCHOR, but amend the protocol to use at least three independently prepared candidate realizations and comparable same-lattice unmodified reactive-core references, reporting between-preparation spread before applying the 3.4% threshold. If axis-specific causal attribution is required, use a single active modifier axis or add matched single-axis controls; the current dual-axis S1C41 composition cannot isolate AC1920 from TK100.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The stated 3.4% falsification resolution is not attainable as specified because M-SWEEP requires only one preparation while the measured E2 realization spread is 2.80-3.57x at 120-130 C. The protocol therefore cannot reliably distinguish a chemistry effect from process-state variation.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Load the audited upstream material structure and chemistry-supported local rheology before ranking candidates or deciding whether one-point shared-shape calibration is admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 anchor, modifier axes, and historical boundary needed to define a candidate experiment without using post-result information.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.reason: Check whether an original E2 isothermal time trajectory exists; this is the least-resolved coordinate and is needed before treating hold stability as transferable to the intended candidate.

tool_trace.reason: Retrieve source-level analogue evidence for sparse local chemistry coverage, while keeping external evidence separate from the local rheological regularities.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: The measured 120-130 C level change against the unmodified reactive core falls within 8.80% of exactly one registered prediction: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. That hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the processing-window level is reported with it.
